title: feat: dashboard calls Gen's account API with a session token
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
The dashboard calls Gen's public account API with a short-lived token, so everything it can do, apps and agents can do with API keys. The account API cleanup it needed shipped separately in #16678.

- Enter mints a 15-minute `sess_` token from the dashboard cookie (`POST /api/session-token`). The dashboard calls `gen.pollinations.ai/account/*` with it
- The dashboard caches the token and drops it when its session check sees a different user, so an account switch in another tab is followed as with the cookie
- Enter's account routes become bearer-only: an API key or a `sess_` token, no cookie
- Account permission checks move to `shared/`, so Gen machines (`/alpha/e2b`) accept the token as the account owner and a dashboard machines page needs no Enter routes
- The usage CSV download fetches with the token instead of following a link
- Tests use an `accountToken` fixture; `session-token.test.ts` covers minting, cookie refusal, and expired, forged or banned-user tokens

**Decisions**

- `account:keys` is account admin and is granted rarely. Moving polli and sandbox logins off it is #16648
- A `sess_` token also works for generation, as the owner. Accepted for now

gist.headline: One account API, many hands
gist.blurb: The dashboard and API clients take the same path to account data. Enter hands the dashboard a short-lived token; Gen handles the account requests.
gist.summary: Enter adds POST /api/session-token to mint a 15-minute sess_ token from the dashboard cookie, letting the dashboard call Gen's public /account/* API while Enter's account routes accept bearer tokens instead of cookies.
gist.impact: Apps and agents can use API keys for the account operations the dashboard uses, while dashboard account switches follow the new user when the session check changes.
gist.visual_concept: Show the dashboard and an app sharing a path to Gen's account API: Polli carries a small token marked '15m' from a cozy Enter terminal across a garden bridge, while a friendly monitor robot holds an API key on the neighboring path. Code-plants and flowers make the shared route legible without implying the token and API key are identical.
